extracted.subtask_description: A general-purpose style and usage guide for Reuters journalists and editors, giving word-by-word entries and rules on grammar, usage, capitalization, spelling, numbers, geography, and reporting practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: each
rubrics_metrics.description: Each takes a singular verb. Be careful when it follows a noun that is the real subject of the sentence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'Each of us is guilty.' Warning: 'We each are guilty' is equivalent to 'We are all guilty' and may be incorrect if 'each' follows a noun that is the real subject.

rubrics_metrics.name: each and every
rubrics_metrics.description: Plain each will do, or plain every.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid redundant 'each and every'; use either 'each' or 'every' depending on context.

rubrics_metrics.name: earth
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally lower case, but capitalise the Planet Earth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capitalize 'Earth' when referring to the planet; otherwise lowercase.

rubrics_metrics.name: earthquakes
rubrics_metrics.description: Use plain 'magnitude' to describe earthquakes; Richter scale is not reliable for certain types and is no longer widely used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer 'moment magnitude' (as used by USGS). Magnitude does not automatically indicate damage; depth and other factors matter. Other scales (Mercalli, Shindo) measure intensity at points. Define 'epicentre' as point on surface above the subterranean centre/focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eastern Rite Churches
rubrics_metrics.description: Churches that returned to communion with Rome after the 1054 split but worship in an Eastern rite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note historical context: each returned to unity with Rome at different times over past 900 years.

rubrics_metrics.name: EBIT
rubrics_metrics.description: Earnings before interest and tax, also called operating earnings.

rubrics_metrics.name: EBITDA
rubrics_metrics.description: Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation, also called core earnings.

rubrics_metrics.name: EBITDAR
rubrics_metrics.description: Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation, amortisation and rent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used instead of EBITDA in industries where equipment or asset rentals figure large (e.g., airlines).

rubrics_metrics.name: EBRD
rubrics_metrics.description: European Bank for Reconstruction and Development, set up to help centrally planned economies move to a free market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owned by governments but invests mainly in private enterprise, usually with commercial partners; operates in 27 countries from central Europe to central Asia.

rubrics_metrics.name: ECB
rubrics_metrics.description: European Central Bank, based in Frankfurt, sets monetary policy for the euro zone countries.

rubrics_metrics.name: effete
rubrics_metrics.description: Means exhausted or sterile, not just weak or foppish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use loosely; use only when meaning exhausted/sterile.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eid al-Adha
rubrics_metrics.description: A Muslim holiday marking the climax of the annual pilgrimage (haj) on the 10th day of the 12th month of the Muslim calendar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eid al-Fitr
rubrics_metrics.description: A Muslim holiday marking the end of the fasting month of Ramadan, the ninth month of the Muslim calendar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eire
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'Republic of Ireland'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer formal country name rather than 'Eire'.

rubrics_metrics.name: either
rubrics_metrics.description: Either is a choice of two things; cannot be used with more than two.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often can be excised. Do not use 'either' when you mean 'each'. Examples given to show incorrect uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: elderly
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid, because the terms are relative and can be inappropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Age descriptors vary by culture; avoid unless precise/necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: -elect
rubrics_metrics.description: Hyphenated and lower case when used as a suffix: e.g. 'President-elect Frederick Green.'

rubrics_metrics.name: election/elections
rubrics_metrics.description: Use singular if it is a single parliamentary election; plural if several votes are taking place contemporaneously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: general election in Britain is singular; US voting on same day for multiple offices are 'elections'.

rubrics_metrics.name: elicit, illicit
rubrics_metrics.description: Elicit = draw forth; illicit = illegal or not permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'A dalliance may elicit an illicit relationship.'

rubrics_metrics.name: ellipsis
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate omission in a quote with three full stops with a space before and after: 'We will fight ... and we will win.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capitalize the word after dots if it starts a new sentence. Only drop words when deletion does not alter the sense of the quote.

rubrics_metrics.name: elusive
rubrics_metrics.description: Usually superfluous and shown by context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'Police are hunting an elusive killer.' Use sparingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: email
rubrics_metrics.description: One word. Other e- prefixed words should be hyphenated (e-commerce, e-banking).

rubrics_metrics.name: embarrass, embarrassed, embarrassing
rubrics_metrics.description: Spell with double r and double s.

rubrics_metrics.name: embargo, boycott
rubrics_metrics.description: An embargo is a legal ban on trade; a boycott is the refusal of a group to deal with a person or use a commodity.

rubrics_metrics.name: embattled
rubrics_metrics.description: A tired cliché. Do not use.

rubrics_metrics.name: emerge
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid phrasing 'It has emerged that' because news does not 'just emerge' without a source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give the reader a clear source for information.

rubrics_metrics.name: emigrate, immigrate
rubrics_metrics.description: You emigrate when you leave a country; you immigrate when you come to a country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similarly use emigrant/immigrant appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: emotive words
rubrics_metrics.description: Some words have emotional significance and must be used with care in the interest of objectivity (e.g., 'terrorist', 'extremist', 'mob').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid contentious labels. Do not adjudicate; use such words only when directly quoting named sources. Use alternatives (gunmen, bombers) or describe actions/aims rather than apply labels.

rubrics_metrics.name: enormity
rubrics_metrics.description: Does not mean just 'very big' but an outrage, iniquity, or great crime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid misuse when intending to say 'very large'.

rubrics_metrics.name: England
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use England as a synonym for Britain or the United Kingdom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'Britain' for England+Scotland+Wales, and 'United Kingdom' to include Northern Ireland; use 'Republic of Ireland' where Irish context is important.

rubrics_metrics.name: en route
rubrics_metrics.description: Two words.

rubrics_metrics.name: enquire, enquiry
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'inquire' and 'inquiry' instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: enrol
rubrics_metrics.description: Use enrol, enrolled, enrolling, enrolment (American style: enroll, enrolling, enrollment).

rubrics_metrics.name: ensure, insure, assure
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Ensure' means to make sure, 'insure' to guarantee against loss, 'assure' to reassure someone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the correct verb for the intended meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: envelop, envelope
rubrics_metrics.description: Verb is 'envelop'; noun is 'envelope'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use correct form: 'enveloping, enveloped' for verbs.

rubrics_metrics.name: envision
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'envisage' instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: epicentre
rubrics_metrics.description: The point on the earth's surface above the centre/focus of an earthquake.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPS
rubrics_metrics.description: Earnings per share: portion of company profit allocated to each outstanding share; indicator of profitability.

rubrics_metrics.name: equal, equalling, equalled
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not write 'more equal' or 'less equal'; use 'more or less equitable' if necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: American style: equal, equaling, equaled.

rubrics_metrics.name: equable, equitable
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Equable' = even/without great variation; 'equitable' = just or fair.

rubrics_metrics.name: equally as
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use together.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use either 'equally bright' or 'as bright'.

rubrics_metrics.name: escalate, escalation
rubrics_metrics.description: Often 'rise' or 'increase' is simpler; 'escalate' may be used for step-by-step increases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer simpler terms unless nuance requires 'escalation'.

rubrics_metrics.name: escapers, not escapees
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer 'escapers' instead of 'escapees'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Esfahan
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'Esfahan', not 'Isfahan', Iran.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eskimo
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use to refer to people of northern Canada; they use 'Inuit'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Singular is 'Inuk'; language is 'Inuktitut'. Use appropriate local names.

rubrics_metrics.name: estimate
rubrics_metrics.description: When referring to economic trends/business performance, use 'estimate' for approximate calculation up to the present; 'forecast' for expected future performance; 'projection' for probable future performance based on current trends/assumptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose term that properly reflects time frame and certainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: estimated at about
rubrics_metrics.description: Tautology; 'estimated at' is sufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid 'estimated at about'.

rubrics_metrics.name: et cetera
rubrics_metrics.description: Use abbreviation 'etc.' with full stop, but try to avoid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer explicit listing or rewriting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethiopian names
rubrics_metrics.description: The word 'ato' meaning 'Mr' should not be used; use only the first name at second reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'Mengistu Haile Mariam – Mengistu said ...'

rubrics_metrics.name: ethnicity
rubrics_metrics.description: See 'race'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implied: treat with care and relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: euphemism
rubrics_metrics.description: Euphemism cloaks reality in innocuous words; avoid it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer direct language: use 'kill' not 'terminate with extreme prejudice'; 'poor' not 'disadvantaged' when appropriate; 'severe storms kill people, not leave them dead.'

rubrics_metrics.name: EU
rubrics_metrics.description: European Union; Treaty on European Union (Maastricht Treaty) created the EU on Nov 1, 1993.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'EU' as the accepted acronym; context on responsibilities beyond EC may be noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: euro
rubrics_metrics.description: No capital letter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eurobond
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalised; bond issued by a country or company in a currency that is not their own.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not to be confused with euro-denominated bonds (issued in euros). Example given.

rubrics_metrics.name: European
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use as a synonym for 'white' in a racial context.

rubrics_metrics.name: European names
rubrics_metrics.description: Use lower case for particles within personal names (de, da, von, van, y), retain particles at second reference in most cases; follow German usage where 'von' is dropped at second reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upper case particles at start of geographical names or start of sentence. Examples provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eurosceptic
rubrics_metrics.description: One word.

rubrics_metrics.name: euro zone
rubrics_metrics.description: Two words, lower case, no hyphen; group of countries that have the euro as their currency.

rubrics_metrics.name: eventuate
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer 'result'.

rubrics_metrics.name: ever
rubrics_metrics.description: Tautology when it follows a superlative (biggest, best).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drop 'ever' unless in direct quotes.

rubrics_metrics.name: every day, everyday
rubrics_metrics.description: Two words for adverb ('every day'); one word for adjective ('everyday').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'Every day we remind him not to wear everyday clothes to a wedding.'

rubrics_metrics.name: everyone, every one
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Everyone' = all the people; 'every one' = every single person (use when you can add 'without exception').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show correct usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: evoke, invoke
rubrics_metrics.description: 'evoke' = bring to mind; 'invoke' = call upon solemnly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'In a speech evoking memories of the civil war he invoked God’s help...'

rubrics_metrics.name: ex-
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefix should be hyphenated to the word it limits; distinction between 'ex-minister' and 'ex-Conservative minister'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer 'former' in written text. 'Ex-' may be used in headlines for brevity.

rubrics_metrics.name: exacerbate
rubrics_metrics.description: Means to make bitter or more violent; often overused or clumsy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usually writers mean simply to 'make worse'. Use precise wording.

rubrics_metrics.name: exactly
rubrics_metrics.description: Cannot be qualified; phrases like 'almost exactly' are not acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: exam
rubrics_metrics.description: Contraction for academic examinations only.

rubrics_metrics.name: execution
rubrics_metrics.description: Use only for lawful killings after due judicial process.

rubrics_metrics.name: except, accept
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Except' = to leave out; 'accept' = to take or receive.

rubrics_metrics.name: excerpt
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'excerpt from', not 'excerpt of'.

rubrics_metrics.name: exchange rates
rubrics_metrics.description: Normally quote a single mid-rate (middle between bid and offer) for value of one currency against another; in forex reports give bid and offer rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rates generally to four decimal places except yen to two. If bid-offer difference odd, quote as near midpoint as possible. Provide examples and rules about formatting, rounding, repeating figures, use of brackets for comparisons, and not running two sets of figures together. Do not round interest rates or company dividends; round other figures as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: exclamation mark, exclamation point
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid except in quotations.

rubrics_metrics.name: expatriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'expatriate' (not 'expatriot').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: But use 'compatriot' for someone of the same country.

rubrics_metrics.name: expect, anticipate
rubrics_metrics.description: Not synonyms: 'anticipate' implies taking precautionary action as well as expectation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the verb that matches intended meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: explicit, implicit
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Explicit' = stated plainly; 'implicit' = implied or suggested.

rubrics_metrics.name: exports overseas
rubrics_metrics.description: Tautology; 'exports' is sufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid redundant phrasing.

rubrics_metrics.name: extra
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not hyphenate when it means 'outside of' unless the prefix is followed by 'a' or a capital letter.

rubrics_metrics.name: extra cover
rubrics_metrics.description: Two words for the field position in cricket.

rubrics_metrics.name: extramarital
rubrics_metrics.description: One word.

rubrics_metrics.name: eyewitness
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer 'witness' instead of 'eyewitness'.

rubrics_metrics.name: FAA
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal Aviation Administration (US).

rubrics_metrics.name: face to face
rubrics_metrics.description: Redundant when used to describe a meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer more specific phrasing.

rubrics_metrics.name: facility
rubrics_metrics.description: Generic word that can mean almost anything; avoid and be specific (base, factory, depot).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be precise about location/function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fahrenheit
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Fahrenheit if it is the local scale, with Celsius conversion in brackets; spell in full at first reference, abbreviate to C and F subsequently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides conversion rules and examples for above/below zero.

rubrics_metrics.name: Falklands
rubrics_metrics.description: Internationally accepted name 'Falkland Islands'; from an Argentine dateline they may be called 'the Malvinas'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the name appropriate to dateline/source.

rubrics_metrics.name: fallacy, fallibility
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Fallacy' = something regarded as true but actually false; 'fallibility' = capacity to make mistakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fallopian tubes
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalize 'Fallopian'.

rubrics_metrics.name: FAO
rubrics_metrics.description: Food and Agriculture Organization (U.N. – Rome).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides website reference: www.fao.org

rubrics_metrics.name: Faroes
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'Faroes', not 'Faeroes'.

rubrics_metrics.name: farther, farthest
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'further, furthest' except when referring to physical distance.

rubrics_metrics.name: fast bowler
rubrics_metrics.description: Two words in cricket.

rubrics_metrics.name: faze, phase
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Faze' = to worry or disturb; 'phase' = a stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: FBI
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal Bureau of Investigation (US). May be used alone at first reference; if full name used at first reference, initials need not be bracketed in.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of US Department of Justice; premier federal law enforcement agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: FCC
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal Communications Commission (U.S.).

rubrics_metrics.name: FDA
rubrics_metrics.description: Food and Drug Administration (U.S.), regulatory body for safety and effectiveness of foods, drugs, medical devices and cosmetics.

rubrics_metrics.name: fears, hopes
rubrics_metrics.description: Unattributed hopes and fears represent opinions and must be sourced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You cannot state 'hopes for a settlement' or 'fears of another oil price increase' without saying who hopes/fears. Exceptions for common humanity or general phrasing allowed; see emotive words.

rubrics_metrics.name: fedayeen
rubrics_metrics.description: Arab or Islamic guerrillas; singular 'feda’i' so use 'guerrilla' for simplicity when referring to one person.

rubrics_metrics.name: feet, foot
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'one foot', 'several feet'. Use 'foot' singular as adjective (a 12-foot-high wall).

rubrics_metrics.name: fellow
rubrics_metrics.description: Often unnecessary, especially before countryman or countrywoman.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid redundant 'fellow' where simple noun suffices.

rubrics_metrics.name: fewer, less than
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'fewer' for numbers of individuals/items; 'less' for quantities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'Fewer than 10 rescuers were hurt' vs 'Less than 1,000 tons of coal was lost.'

rubrics_metrics.name: fiance, fiancee
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Fiance' is the man; 'fiancee' is the woman.

rubrics_metrics.name: fief
rubrics_metrics.description: Not 'fiefdom'.

rubrics_metrics.name: field marshal
rubrics_metrics.description: Note only one 'l'.

rubrics_metrics.name: FIFA
rubrics_metrics.description: International Football Federation (soccer), based in Zurich; can cite www.fifa.com.

rubrics_metrics.name: fighter jets
rubrics_metrics.description: Write 'fighter planes' since modern fighters are almost invariably jets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Always check numbers and ensure internal consistency and feasibility. Use words one to nine in text (except dates/times), numerals for 10 and above, with many exceptions and detailed rules for ages, percentages, dimensions, ordinals, rounding, decimals, ranges, billions/millions formatting, fractions and use of brackets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides extensive rules: spell out digits one-nine except dates/times; use numerals for ages and before millions/billions; use numerals for percentages; repeat figures when unexpected; bracket repeated figures; do not run two sets of figures together; write fractions as 4-1/2 etc.; round off unwieldy figures; round normally to two significant decimals with halves rounded upwards; do not round interest rates or dividends; use full stop as decimal point, comma for thousands; format ranges as '1.2 billion to 1.4 billion' rather than '1.2-1.4 billion'; spell out 'billion' except in headlines, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: filibuster
rubrics_metrics.description: To delay parliamentary proceedings by making long speeches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filipino
rubrics_metrics.description: Native of the Philippines. Feminine 'Filipina'. Plural 'Filipinos, Filipinas'. Adjective is 'Philippine'.

rubrics_metrics.name: film titles
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalise every word in titles of books, films, plays, poems, operas, songs and works of art except conjunctions, articles, particles and short prepositions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same rule for radio and television programmes other than news and current affairs (examples given).

rubrics_metrics.name: finalise
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'complete' or 'finish' instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: financial year
rubrics_metrics.description: Year used for a company's accounting purposes; can be calendar year or a different period (often starting in April).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also called fiscal year; provide preferred terms for clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: firefighter
rubrics_metrics.description: Not 'fireman'.

rubrics_metrics.name: firm
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'firm' only for business partnerships; use 'company' for publicly quoted corporations.

rubrics_metrics.name: first lady
rubrics_metrics.description: Lower case in accordance with American style.

rubrics_metrics.name: first quarter, first-quarter
rubrics_metrics.description: Two words for the noun, one word for the adjective (e.g., 'first-quarter results').

rubrics_metrics.name: first slip
rubrics_metrics.description: Two words for cricket fielding position.

rubrics_metrics.name: First World War
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'World War One', not 'WWI'.

rubrics_metrics.name: fiscal year
rubrics_metrics.description: One-year bookkeeping period or financial year used by a government; varies by country and naming conventions differ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: US fiscal year Oct 1–Sept 30; Japan Apr 1–Mar 31; guidance on writing 'fiscal 2003/04' vs alert/headline abbreviations; prefer 'financial' or 'business year' for companies.

rubrics_metrics.name: flack, flak
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Flack' = American slang term for a public relations person (use only if explained); 'flak' = anti-aircraft fire or heavy criticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: flair, flare
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Flair' = a talent; 'flare' = an illuminating device.

rubrics_metrics.name: flaunt, flout
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Flaunt' = display ostentatiously; 'flout' = defy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'By flaunting your wealth you flout convention.'

rubrics_metrics.name: flay, flail
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Flay' = to flog or subject to savage criticism; 'flail' = to strike or swing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fleet Street
rubrics_metrics.description: No longer a useful synonym for the British press.

rubrics_metrics.name: flight numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: When scheduled flights come into the news (crashes, hijackings), give the flight number together with other identification such as type of aircraft, airline, destination and route.

rubrics_metrics.name: flounder, founder
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Flounder' = a fish or to struggle violently; 'founder' = to subside, sink or collapse.

rubrics_metrics.name: flyer
rubrics_metrics.description: Not 'flier'; in American style use 'flier' for both aviator and handbill. Some trains/buses use 'flyer' as part of proper name.

rubrics_metrics.name: flyhalf
rubrics_metrics.description: One word for rugby position.

rubrics_metrics.name: focus, focused
rubrics_metrics.description: Use sparingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: following
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer 'after' as a preposition (e.g., 'After the crash...' not 'Following the crash...').

rubrics_metrics.name: follow up, follow-up
rubrics_metrics.description: Two words for the verb; one word for the noun and adjective.

rubrics_metrics.name: foodstuffs, supplies
rubrics_metrics.description: In most cases 'food' is enough.

rubrics_metrics.name: foot
rubrics_metrics.description: To convert to metres roughly multiply by 3 and divide by 10; precise multiply by 0.305.

rubrics_metrics.name: foot-and-mouth disease
rubrics_metrics.description: Retain the hyphenation even if used alone without the noun; not 'hoof-and-mouth'.

rubrics_metrics.name: forbear, forebear
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Forbear' = to abstain; 'forebear' = an ancestor.

rubrics_metrics.name: forced
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not say people were 'forced' to act (troops forced to open fire) as it implies judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid wording that implies editorial judgment about motivation/actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: forecast
rubrics_metrics.description: Past tense is 'forecast', not 'forecasted'.

rubrics_metrics.name: forego, forgo
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Forego' = to precede; 'forgo' = to do without.

rubrics_metrics.name: forehand
rubrics_metrics.description: One word in tennis.

rubrics_metrics.name: foreign language phrases
rubrics_metrics.description: Use foreign phrases only in exceptional cases where no recognised English equivalent exists; they must always be explained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example given with Latin phrase and translation.

rubrics_metrics.name: foreign exchange rates
rubrics_metrics.description: Use mid-rate in general news stories; see Exchange Rates entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: forensic
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Forensic' = of or used in courts of law. Do not use 'forensic examination' when you mean 'examination by forensic scientists.'

rubrics_metrics.name: forex
rubrics_metrics.description: Abbreviation for foreign exchange; can be used in headlines for space constraints; otherwise use full description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also a club grouping foreign exchange dealers with local forex clubs in major centres.

rubrics_metrics.name: former, latter
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid these expressions as they force readers to read backwards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer clearer wording that names the subjects.

rubrics_metrics.name: formula, formulas
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'formulas', not 'formulae'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formula One
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalised in motor sport.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fort
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not abbreviate in names of cities or military installations (e.g. 'Fort Lauderdale').

rubrics_metrics.name: fortnight
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer 'two weeks'.

rubrics_metrics.name: fortuitous, fortunate
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Fortuitous' = by chance; 'fortunate' = lucky.

rubrics_metrics.name: forward
rubrics_metrics.description: Not 'forwards'.

rubrics_metrics.name: foul, fowl
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Foul' = dirty/disfigured/sport infraction; 'fowl' = a bird.

rubrics_metrics.name: four-wheel drive
rubrics_metrics.description: Not '4x4' unless part of a proper name.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fourth of July
rubrics_metrics.description: Or 'July Fourth' for the U.S. holiday.

rubrics_metrics.name: fractions
rubrics_metrics.description: Where precision not essential, use 'a quarter', 'a third' rather than percentages; precise figures should appear lower in the story. Do not mix decimals and fractions in the same sentence. Hyphenate fractional compounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example guidance for opinion poll leads vs detailed reporting; hyphenation rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frankenstein
rubrics_metrics.description: Frankenstein is the creator, not the monster.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freddie Mac
rubrics_metrics.description: Acceptable at first reference; put full title 'Federal Home Mortgage Corp.' later in the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: free kick
rubrics_metrics.description: Two words.

rubrics_metrics.name: french fries
rubrics_metrics.description: Lower case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frisbee
rubrics_metrics.description: (trade mark)

rubrics_metrics.name: front line
rubrics_metrics.description: Two words as noun; but 'front-line' as adjective.

rubrics_metrics.name: FSA
rubrics_metrics.description: Financial Services Authority, the British regulator for most financial services markets, exchanges and firms.

rubrics_metrics.name: FTC
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal Trade Commission (U.S.).

rubrics_metrics.name: fuel, fuelled / fuel, fueling
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'fuel, fuelled' (British) but in American style use 'fuel, fueling, fueled'.

rubrics_metrics.name: fulfil, fulfilling, fulfilled
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'fulfil' and related forms; 'fulfilment' is noun.

rubrics_metrics.name: full
rubrics_metrics.description: Hyphenate when forming compound words (full-length, full-service).

rubrics_metrics.name: fulsome
rubrics_metrics.description: Not 'fullsome'; 'fulsome praise' is excessive and fawning, not simply lavish.

rubrics_metrics.name: fundamentalist
rubrics_metrics.description: One who believes literal truth of sacred texts; now often used for extreme political and religious views and has disparaging overtones — use with care.

rubrics_metrics.name: fundraiser, fundraising
rubrics_metrics.description: One word.

rubrics_metrics.name: fused participles
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid fused participles; rewrite to make objects/actors explicit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: rewrite 'The bank tried to prevent him selling' to 'The bank tried to prevent him from selling.'

rubrics_metrics.name: furlough
rubrics_metrics.description: Not 'furlow'.

rubrics_metrics.name: future plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Tautology; use 'plans' instead of 'future plans'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remove redundant 'future' from 'future prospects' and 'future hopes'.

rubrics_metrics.name: G3, G5, G7, G8, G10, G24, G30, G77
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries defining various international groupings (G3, G5, G7, G8, G10, G24, G30, G77) and their membership/role.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each entry explains membership and purpose, e.g., G7 members, G8 includes Russia, G10 works within IMF, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: GAO
rubrics_metrics.description: Government Accountability Office (U.S.), formerly the General Accounting Office; can be abbreviated to GAO in headlines or at second reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gaborone
rubrics_metrics.description: Not 'Gabarone' (Botswana).

rubrics_metrics.name: gaff, gaffe
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Gaff' = a hook; 'gaffe' = a mistake.

rubrics_metrics.name: gage, gauge
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Gage' = a pledge or guarantee; 'gauge' = a standard or means of measurement.

rubrics_metrics.name: gales
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'gales' rather than 'gale-force winds'; a gale is less powerful than a storm in nautical parlance.

rubrics_metrics.name: gallon
rubrics_metrics.description: Conversion guidance: Imperial to litres and US to litres conversions with precise multipliers provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives rough and precise conversion methods between Imperial and US gallons and litres and between Imperial and US gallons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gambia
rubrics_metrics.description: Not 'the Gambia, West Africa'.

rubrics_metrics.name: gambit
rubrics_metrics.description: Not simply an opening move (in chess or metaphorically) but one that involves a sacrifice or concession.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid tautology such as 'opening gambit'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gandhi
rubrics_metrics.description: Not 'Ghandi'.

rubrics_metrics.name: gantlet, gauntlet
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'gantlet' for running the gantlet (military punishment); 'gauntlet' for an iron glove.

rubrics_metrics.name: gaol
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'jail'.

rubrics_metrics.name: gas
rubrics_metrics.description: Be careful: 'gas' can mean gases/gassing/gassed; 'gasoline' (US) is 'petrol' in Europe. Do not use 'gas' as synonym for 'gasoline' where ambiguous.

rubrics_metrics.name: gay
rubrics_metrics.description: Now universally used as synonym for homosexual; do not use it in other senses.

rubrics_metrics.name: gearing
rubrics_metrics.description: An indicator of a company's ability to service its debt; explain if used in financial stories but best avoided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See glossary of financial terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: GDP
rubrics_metrics.description: See 'gross domestic product'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geneva Conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Plural.

rubrics_metrics.name: gender
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use language that perpetuates sexual, racial, religious or other stereotypes; cite gender, race, religion, nationality, sexual orientation or marital status only if relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid assuming roles (police/firefighters/soldiers are not necessarily men); use same terms for men and women (mayor, poet), not gendered forms; consider placement of identifying information in story.

rubrics_metrics.name: general (military ranks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Military ranks should never be abbreviated and should be capitalised when referring to a specific individual; follow local practice for hyphenation and translation for non-English ranks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At second reference, use surname OR his/her rank (not both). Examples and note on U.S./British rank stars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gentile
rubrics_metrics.description: Anyone not a Jew, or not a Mormon. Capitalise.

rubrics_metrics.name: generation -- first/second
rubrics_metrics.description: Take care with 'first'/'second' when qualifying immigrants since terms are ambiguous (first-generation may mean immigrants themselves or children of immigrants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be precise about intended meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: geriatrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Medical care of the elderly; 'geriatrics' as noun and 'geriatric' as adjective; does not simply mean 'elderly'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Germany
rubrics_metrics.description: United Germany formally called 'Federal Republic of Germany'; use 'East Germany' for former Communist state, but 'eastern/western Germany' for parts of unified Germany.

rubrics_metrics.name: German spellings
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate umlaut by adding an 'e' after the vowel in inflected forms (von Weizsaecker not von Weizsaecker example).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Fuehrer not Fuhrer.

rubrics_metrics.name: get, got
rubrics_metrics.description: There is always a stronger verb — find it and use it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer more precise vocabulary over 'get/got'.

rubrics_metrics.name: GI, GIs
rubrics_metrics.description: A U.S. soldier (from 'government issue'); use only in informal contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: giant
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use when describing companies; in general avoid the adjective.

rubrics_metrics.name: gibe, gybe, jibe
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'gibe' is a taunt, 'gybe' is to swing a sail over, 'jibe' is to agree (American usage differs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note American vs British usage distinctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gibraltar, Strait of
rubrics_metrics.description: Not 'Straits'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gipsy / Gypsy
rubrics_metrics.description: See 'Gypsy' entry (not fully presented in chunk).

rubrics_metrics.name: girl
rubrics_metrics.description: Any female older than 18 is a woman not a girl. Use 'woman' not 'lady'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid 'girl' for adult females; similarly, use 'man' for males older than 18.
